RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel proves nothing on its own — it's common in senior public-sector recruitment and is consistent with both fair and unfair outcomes. Led as your main argument, it looks like an inference from identity and is easy to dismiss. Mention it only as context, after the substance.

The substance is stronger: on paper your qualifications appear at least equal, the stated reason ("experience of leading international projects") is vague, and your request for written reasons has gone unanswered for two weeks. In many jurisdictions, an unexplained decision plus an apparently equally or better qualified candidate of the other sex can shift the burden of proof onto the employer.

Chase the written reasons formally, in writing, with a deadline. Then assess.
